rapport_notes: Warm and empathetic, especially responding to the customer's past bad experience with damage.

evidence_quotes.agenda: "What are the biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today. Aside from the rate, the pricing?"
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'making sure things are packed well and no scratches or damages'; rep followed up with 'have you had an experience in the past where in you know, your item got damaged?' -- a genuine second-layer question that surfaced a past bad experience, which rep then addressed directly with the damage-coverage answer.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: N/A -- call diverted to walkthrough scheduling before Stage 3 was reached.

top_strength: Turned a generic damage-concern into a real two-layer discovery moment by asking about past experience, then tied the $2,000 coverage benefit directly to that specific worry.
coaching_note: Give the quid pro quo framing a clear time-box (e.g. 'six minutes') -- it explained what info was needed but never set an expectation for how long.
